studies.Population: Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk in Limburg province
studies.Ethnicity Basis: Default: no protocol-mapped specific country or population was established
studies.Reference: Dietary intake of micronutrients and the risk of developing bladder cancer: results from the Belgian case-control study on bladder cancer risk.
studies.Authors: Brinkman MT, Buntinx F, Kellen E, Dagnelie PC, Van Dongen MC, Muls E, Zeegers MP
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: The IMMIDIET standardized food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was sent by mail to all participants in the study.

sample_size.excerpt: Therefore, dietary data from a total of 198 cases and 377 controls were included in the analyses of this study. Table 1 presents the study characteristics of the participants in the Belgian case–control study on bladder cancer.
sample_size.location: Results, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 198 + 377 = 575

design.excerpt: Briefly, our study was a population-based case–control study conducted in the Belgian province of Limburg consisting of 200 bladder cancer cases and 386 healthy control subjects

timing.excerpt: Participants were asked to report their usual dietary intake for the 12 months prior to the interview.

continent.excerpt: A semi-quantitative 322 item food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was used to collect dietary data from 200 bladder cancer cases and 386 control subjects participating in the Belgian case–control study on bladder cancer risk.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The IMMIDIET standardized food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) was sent by mail to all participants in the study.
